paper.title_en: Polarized solid target for possible future AMBER program at CERN
paper.abstract_en: A possible physics program for the second phase of the AMBER experiment at CERN is being explored, with a focus on measurements of transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution functions (TMD PDFs), such as the Sivers, Transversity and Boer-Mulders functions, using a transversally polarized solid target. The COMPASS experiment previously showed that the available data favor the theoretical prediction of a sign reversal of the Sivers function between the Drell-Yan and SIDIS processes, while the question is not yet fully settled due to limited statistical accuracy. The AMBER experimental setup exploits the flexibility of the CERN SPS M2 beam line, allowing the use of both positive and negative pion beams, and foresees an increase in beam intensity, which would require upgrades to the existing polarized target system. Operation at higher beam intensities introduces challenges such as localized heating and radiation damage, potentially affecting target polarization stability. To address these issues, three possible scenarios for improvements of the polarized target system are discussed, including operation with continuous dynamic nuclear polarization during data taking or a substantial extension of the polarization relaxation time in frozen-spin mode, enabling stable measurements with higher experimental accuracy at high beam intensities. In addition, developments such as a streaming data-acquisition system and a dedicated vertex detector are expected to increase the collected statistics through a reduction of trigger dead time, while further enhancing mass resolution and background rejection, thereby extending the accessible dilepton mass range down to about 4 GeV.
